classification.difficultyReason: Use a cosine-rule angle and a midpoint length to calculate the first median, then transfer that scaffolded method to two newly constructed midpoint triangles.

content.prompt: In $\triangle ABC$, $AB=6\text{ cm}$, $AC=10\text{ cm}$, $BC=14\text{ cm}$ and $X$ is the midpoint of side $BC$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find, correct to one decimal place:

answer.worked:
$CX=7\text{ cm}$ because $X$ is the midpoint of $BC$. Since $\angle ACX=\angle ACB$, use the exact value $\cos\angle ACX=\frac{13}{14}$.

$$\begin{align*}AX^2&=10^2+7^2-2\times10\times7\times\frac{13}{14}\\AX^2&=19\\AX&=\sqrt{19}\text{ cm}\\AX&\approx4.4\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

inlines.text: of the triangle. A median is the line segment from a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side.
Find the length of the other two medians, correct to one decimal place.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with horizontal CB, A above the base, median AX, matching single ticks on CX and XB, and a red midpoint X. No numerical measurements are printed.
spec.mathematics: X is the midpoint of BC; CX=XB and AX joins A to X. Coordinates are derived from the given side lengths.
spec.answerVisibility: All labels, midpoint ticks and the median are permanent question givens; no calculated answers appear.

answer.short:
The median from $B$ is $9.5\text{ cm}$; the median from $C$ is $11.8\text{ cm}$.

Bisect the relevant side and apply the cosine rule.
answer.worked:
Let $D$ be the midpoint of $AC$ and $E$ the midpoint of $AB$. Then $AD=5\text{ cm}$ and $BE=3\text{ cm}$.

For the median from $B$:

$$\begin{align*}\cos A&=\frac{6^2+10^2-14^2}{2\times6\times10}\\\cos A&=-\frac12\\BD^2&=6^2+5^2-2\times6\times5\times\left(-\frac12\right)\\BD^2&=91\\BD&=\sqrt{91}\text{ cm}\\BD&\approx9.5\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

For the median from $C$:

$$\begin{align*}\cos B&=\frac{6^2+14^2-10^2}{2\times6\times14}\\\cos B&=\frac{11}{14}\\CE^2&=14^2+3^2-2\times14\times3\times\frac{11}{14}\\CE^2&=139\\CE&=\sqrt{139}\text{ cm}\\CE&\approx11.8\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
